lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Rebuilt weekly carrier scorecards used by 6 regional managers to renegotiate contracts, cutting late deliveries from 11% to 7% in two quarters.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites; my redesign of the slotting rules was rolled out with the floor supervisors and 45 retrained pickers.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Use actual contact details and a working profile link if these are not placeholders.
items.because: Recruiters need to reach you.

items.says: Make the MBA completion status unambiguous.
items.because: The date implies completion without explicitly confirming it.

items.says: Put Harbor Payments before Crestline Logistics.
items.because: The experience section should run in reverse chronological order.

items.says: Be ready to explain the move from the MBA and product internship into mechanic work.
items.because: The chronology will prompt that question.

items.says: Clarify whether under five days applies to every job or is an average or target.
items.because: The distinction matters to the result's credibility.

items.says: Add a substantiated scale or outcome for the winch work.
items.because: The bullet describes responsibilities rather than their effect.

items.says: Clarify your contribution to the drop in late deliveries.
items.because: Scorecards used in renegotiations may not explain the full drop on their own.

items.says: Clarify the measurement period for the 30% reduction.
items.because: It would make the result easier to evaluate.

items.says: Clarify your ownership of the redesign versus the rollout.
items.because: It would make the result easier to evaluate.

items.says: Specify whether forecast error was measured consistently before and after.
items.because: The 18%-to-11% result is meaningful only with the same measure.

items.says: Split or narrow the route-planning bullet's scope.
items.because: The many activities make it hard to see what produced the 1,800-hour saving.

items.says: Clarify the period measured for the onboarding result.
Clarify whether all 2,300 merchants were exposed to the new process.
Call the change from 61% to 66% a five-percentage-point increase.
items.because: It is not a 5% relative increase.

items.says: Reach is misapplied by scoring it as support tickets a feature might close.
items.because: Those tickets are not necessarily the number of people or cases it would reach.

items.says: Shorten the chain of activities.
Clarify whether the team adopted the roadmap priority.
items.because: “Set” may imply decision authority you did not have.

items.says: Combine this A/B-test information with the checkout-conversion bullet or remove one.
items.because: The bullets substantially overlap.

items.says: The bullet presents a session-measured effect as an effect on customers.
items.because: An effect measured on sessions must be distinguished from one on individual customers or merchants.

items.says: Clarify whether funding was approved, committed, or actually spent.
items.because: The rollout claim should be precise.

items.says: Confirm that “Present” is accurate and clarify your current involvement if the project is ongoing.
items.because: The MBA has ended.

items.says: Check that the nine tonnes represents measured redistribution.
Avoid assuming that all nine tonnes would otherwise have been discarded.
items.because: That assumption may be unverifiable.

items.says: The increase from 400 to 1,150 weekly active users is 187.5%, not 150%.
Do not attribute the entire user gain to reminders without supporting evidence.
The increase from 75% to 95% is 20 percentage points, not 20%.
Support the connection between the volunteer system and the fill-rate result.
Briefly clarify the scheduling-savings model's basis.
Change the passive construction.
items.because: It is less informative than the surrounding bullets.

items.says: Specify your team's contribution to the intake changes.
items.because: It is less informative than the surrounding bullets.

items.says: Give a concrete effect of the intake changes if one was measured.
items.because: It is less informative than the surrounding bullets.

items.says: Consolidate the pilot-approval story or distinguish the two decisions.
items.because: The outcome overlaps the preceding scheduling-savings bullet.

items.says: Ensure the roadmapping skill is backed by an example you can discuss.
items.because: The RICE bullet could undermine the claim of roadmapping expertise.

items.says: Add relevant tools if you have used them proficiently.
items.because: The current list is thin for some product roles.
